cohort: The study included 240 pregnant women (120 preeclamptic, 120 normotensive) between 28-36 weeks of gestation.
finding: Preeclamptic women had significantly lower serum calcium and magnesium levels compared to normotensive women, with deficiencies associated with preeclampsia severity and poor pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: Lower serum calcium and magnesium levels were associated with higher cesarean rates.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken between 28-36 weeks of gestation, and pregnancy outcomes were assessed at birth.
